title: A guarded column is lazy over column operands
verdict: passes for operands that read a column
description: `pl.when(r).then(p).otherwise(None)` over stacked `with_columns`, on the streaming engine with the default optimizations: `p` (a strict cast of the text `bad`) raises on no row where `r` is FALSE, for every case probed with a column operand: a stacked chain of 4 levels read plainly, under a selective filter on `id`, under a filter on the chain's value, under an aggregate, and with a reach that is FALSE on every row by data only (`s IS NULL AND s IS NOT NULL`). The rows match the reference. A constant-only operand is the exception: see polars-exec-when-eager.
reference: `CASE WHEN r THEN p END` evaluates `p` only where `r` holds, also over stacked projections (`Expr.issues`: an `ifThen` raises what its taken branch raises). A guarded column of the D50-d chain therefore raises on no row whose reach is FALSE.

evidence.note: `python -m sverify_dev.guarded_columns p1 --engine polars`: Polars 2.1.0 (Python), streaming engine, Linux x86_64 (homelab); the P1 cases also ran on macOS arm64 for DuckDB and Polars with the same result.

provenance.notes: Issue #1719 (D50-d). Probe rows: 3000, every third one the text `bad`, which a strict cast rejects.
